title: Holdfast onramp playflows and telemetry hypotheses (draft)
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight working doc for a minimal, empirically-driven SDK onramp were calling "Holdfast" (small number of high-confidence steps that anchor a new developer). Purpose is to reduce cognitive load for the critical first 10 minutes, and to instrument that path so we can verify hypotheses about dropoff and time-to-first-success.

Audience:
- DX engineers shipping quickstart flows and starter examples
- SDK docs writers and sampleapp maintainers
- Solutions engineers who run onboarding labs

Design constraints (quick, composable, low-maintenance):
- Keep sample app ~50 LOC for main path (clonable + run with 1 env var)
- No heavy infra required (local mode + token only; optional sandbox script for more advanced flows)
- Instrument three measurable events (see Telemetry section)
- Failure surface should map to a single remediation step (surface actionable error strings)

Hypotheses (to validate):
H1: Developers who complete the Holdfast path in <= 10 minutes are 3x more likely to try a second sample.
H2: Reducing visible steps from 7 -> 3 (explicit checklist items) reduces abandonment at step 2 by 40%.
H3: Time to first token (TTFT) is correlated with perceived success more than total tokens consumed.

Holdfast minimal flow (3 checkpoints):
1) Clone + install (0-2 min)
   - git clone + pip/npx install (one line script provided)
   - Set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var (copy paste)
2) Run sample: simple chat/generate (2-6 min)
   - single command: run hello-world (starts local server or prints sample output)
   - Show streaming example and non-streaming fallback (explain differences in 1 sentence)
3) Inspect output + tweak (6-10 min)
   - Change the prompt or param (max_tokens/temperature) and re-run
   - Quick note on cost estimate (token counter in CLI output)

Developer-facing copy (for README snippet):
- HEADLINE: "From zero to a running Redwood call in 3 commands"
- 1-liner: "Clone, set your REDWOOD_API_KEY, run: hello-world -- youll see a streaming reply and token cost estimate."

Telemetry / Instrumentation (must be lightweight and privacy-safe):
Key instrumentation points (events):
- event.onramp.clone (timestamp)
- event.onramp.first_request_sent (timestamp, sdk_lang, local_mode_bool)
- event.onramp.first_response_token (timestamp, ttft_ms)
- event.onramp.onramp_complete (timestamp, success_bool, steps_completed)
- Properties: anonymized_id (UUID hashed), sample_variant (hello-stream / hello-sync), env (sandbox|prod).

Success metrics to collect (aggregate):
- median time from clone -> first_response_token (TTFT)
- abandonment rate between clone -> first_request, first_request -> first_response_token
- percent of devs who modify prompt within 10 minutes (proxy: subsequent first_request_sent events)
- error taxonomy counts (auth, network, sample-bug, rate-limit)

Telemetry hypotheses (to test):
T1: TTFT median > 1200ms in local-sim correlates with higher support tickets for confusion about streaming.
T2: >60% of onramp failures are auth-related (bad key) and can be mitigated by a pre-run key-check step.

Sampling & privacy notes:
- Do not capture prompt text. Capture only event names and high-level properties (lengths, hashes).
- Offer an opt-out via --telemetry=off for sample runs.

Playbook for implementers (short checklist):
- [ ] Write the one-line install + run script (keeps to 3 commands)
- [ ] Add explicit auth test: redwood whoami -> friendly error + troubleshooting link
- [ ] Hook 3 telemetry events to the SDK quickstart flow
- [ ] Add token counter to sample CLI output
- [ ] Create an A/B sample variant: streaming-first vs sync-first (for experiments)
- [ ] Draft README microcopy and badge (onramp success badge for README)
- [ ] Add a single failing-case example and recommended fix in docs (copy/paste)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How opinionated should default param values be? (low temp vs exploratory)
- Do we include a built-in mock mode to speed TTFT while still showing streaming?
- Where does the trial sandbox live? a shared sandbox key might reduce friction but increases risk.

Runbook snippets (developer troubleshooting):
- If redwood whoami fails with 401: run "echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | redwood doctor" and link to token rotation doc.
- If first_request_sent but no response: ask dev to run with --verbose and paste a trace id to support (traces: trace-redwood-XXXX).
- If streaming starts then stalls: small helper to detect EOF vs long-poll timeout and show quick fix (reduce batch size or set streaming=true/false).

Experiment plan (2-week cadence):
Week 0: ship Holdfast minimal flow to docs + sample repo (internal beta).
Week 1: collect telemetry (anonymized), run quick funnel analysis on TTFT and abandon rates.
Week 2: iterate on friction points: add pre-run auth test if auth failures > 50%; tweak copy if drop at step 1 still high.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep samples in multiple langs but ensure the canonical 3-command path is identical across languages (shell alias + env var).
- Lean into streaming in the demo but have sync fallback to avoid platform-specific streaming issues.
- Coordinate with infra to expose a lightweight sandbox key for workshops (expires after 24h).

Links & references:
- Quick measurement dashboard (internal): confluence.redwood/display/DEV/Holdfast+Dashboard
- Related tickets: ENG-4821 (onramp telemetry), DX-303 (hello-world refactor)

TO DO (next steps):
- Diego: prototype one-line script and PR sample repo -> due 2026-03-17
- Samantha: draft README microcopy + troubleshooting snippets -> due 2026-03-15
- Elliot: telemetry events + dashboard prototype -> due 2026-03-22

End of draft. This doc is intentionally terse; expand the troubleshooting section if we see recurring support patterns during the beta.
